content:
At the moment, some mathlib dependencies are pinned to the v4.31.0-rc1 tag while others point to their main branches. In theory, all the dependencies could be pointed to the v4.31.0-rc1 tag since they're all part of the lean release cycle. They could also all be pointed to the respective main branches, to make updating them easier in-between the big toolchain bumps. A third option would be to pin them to the version tag on every toolchain bump, and switch them over to their main branches whenever they need to be updated in-between toolchain bumps.

It seems like it would make sense to unify how the dependencies are handled, but I'm unsure which option would make the most sense. With the automated dependency bump PRs, maybe we should just point them all to their respective main branches? @Marcelo Lynch

This issue was originally mentioned by @Jovan Gerbscheid in #40295.

The main advantage of pointing them all to their main branches is that we don't need to wait a whole month to get e.g. the new batteries features in mathlib.

Another advantage is that we can do mathlib adaptations throughout the month, instead of these needing to be part of the big toolchain bump.

I guess we can rely on the "update dependencies" automation to start with, and if we notice this requires manual intervention all the time we can maybe switch to updating via hopscotch? Or is it the norm that we need adaptations in mathlib when updating these dependencies?
Ah, sorry, I thought #40295 was merged. My message assumes a world where we are tracking the latest master for these

Am I right that there aren't really any downsides to pointing all of the dependencies to main / master? The "update dependencies" automation will let us know within a few hours if something breaks mathlib, and if we want we could also install something like !downstream-check on those dependencies so that when PRs are made there they could check if they break mathlib before merging.

Update dependencies just opens a PR after calling lake update, I think...? But yeah the PR CI would break if anything is wrong. I mean that we could tack hopscotch on those failures if we really want the bisection logic (but maybe it will be mostly fine and it's overkill to do that now?)
Re !downstream-check: I guess batteries at least already does this
I can't really think of a downside either.
OK, if @Jovan Gerbscheid reopens #40295 (possibly changing the rest of the dependencies to main as well?) then I'll merge it.
Should we call lake update on that same PR? I guess we can wait for the automation to see how it looks
